title: About the Conference
paragraphs: The 1st International Conference on Soft Computing Application in Smart grid and Renewable Energy (SAGAR-27) will be held on February 26-27 at ABIT Campus jointly by the Electrical Engineering and Electrical and Computer Engineering of ABIT.

Soft Computing Application in Smart grid and Renewable Energy is an important research area in science and engineering in the future. Soft computing techniques focus on approximate models and aim to provide solutions to complex problems. These algorithms aim to be tolerant of imprecision, uncertainty, partial truth, and approximation. Soft computing is the subject of both theoretical and practical research. Soft computing techniques are currently being applied in many applications in areas such as industrial systems, commercial, or domestic applications.

Soft computing covers the fusion of research in evolutionary algorithms and genetic programming neural science and neural net systems, fuzzy set theory and fuzzy systems, chaos theory and chaotic systems, optimization, data Science, data analytics and machine learning.

At the same time, the rapid evolution of electric power systems into smart grids has fundamentally transformed the generation, transmission, distribution, and consumption of electrical energy. Smart grids integrate advanced communication, sensing, control, and protection technologies to ensure reliable, efficient, and sustainable power delivery. With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources, electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and distributed generation, modern power systems have become highly complex, dynamic, and data-driven. In this scenario, soft computing techniques play a crucial role in addressing the planning, operation, optimization, and control challenges of smart grid systems.

Renewable energy has emerged as a cornerstone of sustainable development and clean energy transition worldwide. Sources such as solar, wind, hydro, biomass, and hybrid renewable systems are being increasingly integrated into modern power systems to reduce carbon emissions, enhance energy security, and promote environmental sustainability. However, the intermittent and stochastic nature of renewable energy generation introduces significant technical challenges in forecasting, grid integration, power quality management, energy storage coordination, and real-time control. Advanced soft computing and intelligent optimization techniques provide powerful tools for renewable energy modelling, maximum power extraction, energy management, fault diagnosis, and reliability enhancement in renewable-dominated smart grids.

The SAGAR-27 conference offers an important place for people to share knowledge, work together, and come up with new ideas in soft computing techniques and smart grid technologies since participants will learn about the latest advancements and future trends.
